observations: The opensip-platform package purpose still reads 'OS mechanisms behind explicit interfaces, without policy authority', while two service rows - work_ledger.rs from v61 and now work_reader.rs - are generic bookkeeping rather than OS mechanisms. The tension arrived with the ledger and the packages body is byte-equal here, so it is out of scope, but the purpose line reads more loosely with each generic helper and is worth revisiting in whatever unit next touches the package graph.

The src description says the reader 'preserves errors', meaning the error value. Per audit 429 and my correction, this reader's errors latch the owner, which is why it cannot be dropped into the native read_one bracket. The explicit disclaimer of required postchecks keeps the row honest, but a skim of the first clause could read it as composable error semantics.

The src description is specific about algorithm behavior (charging before requested growth and every read attempt). Selecting a row description is not source approval and the README says so, but the specificity means a later reader should not treat the row as settled behavior for source430.
12 of 12 */tests/*.rs rows now satisfy the <subject>_tests.rs convention; the inventory60 finding has become a habit rather than a one-off correction.
crates/platform/tests/ now holds two integration targets, so the convention there is established for future platform helpers.
